findings.evidence: "Every `Bash` call starts a fresh shell, so every `$TOOLS_PY`/`$CLI_PROFILES_DIR`/`$RUNTIMES_JSON` below means 'the literal path captured here'". Several NEVER items are also repeated almost word for word inside the steps (for example the target announcement at line 35 and line 201, and the purpose rule at line 295 and line 322).
findings.fix: Keep each rule's full wording in one place, either the NEVER list or the step, and have the other place point to it. Shorten the fresh-shell explanation to one clause. Record each shortened passage as a record row.

findings.evidence: Step 2 sends question order to references/wizard-flow.md but keeps Steps 2.3–2.8 inline as long rule paragraphs, so the Process pattern's phase checkpoints are spread across two files without an explicit checklist
findings.fix: Add a short progress checklist at the top of ## Workflow (Step 0 locate → 1 detect/check-providers → 1.5 catalog → 1.6 sort → 2.1 target announced → 2.2 sets confirmed → 2.5 tests → 3 render-toml exit 0 → 4 report/trust/cleanup) so each phase gate is visible

findings.evidence: Some NEVER items give their reason only in a parenthetical, or give none: "Never hand-write a `command` for a runtime the runner knows" states the rule but not what breaks (the entry needs trust and goes stale when the runner's argv changes)
findings.fix: Add the non-obvious consequence to each NEVER item that lacks one. For example: a hand-written command makes the lane command-bearing, so the whole local [lanes] table needs trust, and it stops following runner argv fixes.

findings.evidence: The description is 1013 of the 1024 allowed characters. It starts with "Sets up..." and spends space on implementation detail ("asks each role's order, effort and opt-in flags").
findings.fix: Use this skill to set up, refresh or check ai-kit's cross-AI lanes: which models review plans, which implement them, and each role's fallback order, written to the [lanes] table of ./.aikit/config.toml (or the user config.toml with --global). Use when the user wants cross-AI review or execute lanes, a second-opinion reviewer from another vendor or a fallback executor, even without the word lanes; when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers reports that no lanes exist; to find lane providers opencode no longer lists; or to migrate an old review-spec.toml. --check-only reports availability and writes nothing; --local and --global pick the target but never consent to replace a roster. Not for running a review or execute, hand-editing one lane value, or editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.

findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 418 lines but about 43 KB (roughly 10k tokens), double the recommended 5000-token body. Steps 2.1 (lines 192-199), 2.5 (line 275), 2.7 (line 320) and 2.8 are single paragraphs of several hundred words each.
findings.fix: Move the detailed branch text of Step 2.1 (the replacement gate's answer forms), Step 2.7 (host-precedence detail and the claude-alias entry shape) and Step 2.8 (timeout_tiers detail) into references/ files. Read each one at the step that needs it, and keep a 2-3 line rule summary inline.

findings.evidence: There are 21 evals with verifiable assertions and 22 trigger queries (12 positive, 10 negative). Most edge-case evals have `"files": []` and describe environment state only in the prompt, for example edge-opencode-not-installed-config-fallback, which describes the opencode.jsonc in prose.
findings.fix: Add input fixtures under evals/files/ for the evals that depend on file content. For example, add an opencode.jsonc with provider `mine` for edge-opencode-not-installed-config-fallback, and list each fixture in that eval's files array.

findings.evidence: Step 0 tries the sibling directory, then `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, then `$HOME/.claude/skills/ai-kit-spec-review`. It has no candidate for an opencode, codex or ~/.agents install, so when the skill is installed without its sibling on a non-Claude host, Step 0 stops with 'module is missing' even though ai-kit-spec-review is installed.
findings.fix: Use the same candidate list as ai-kit-spec-review's own resolver, including the host skill directories ai-kit installs to on other runtimes. Otherwise, before stopping, say which paths were tried and ask the owner for the ai-kit-spec-review directory.

findings.evidence: One paragraph carries --catalog-path recording, the usability object semantics, the --extra-json contents, the effort refusal, the review capability string and the Step 4 capability lines. Following the test step means untangling six rules from one block.
findings.fix: Split Step 2.5's test paragraph into a short ordered list: (1) the command, (2) what --extra-json carries and the reason effort is excluded, (3) how to read available/detail, (4) how to read usability.recorded, (5) the capability string for review lanes.
